decisions.rationale: Verified on the bytes at 7e1a2af6. Part (2) holds by code inspection: in tests/layout.test.mjs the finish step loops only over the quiet list, which is the gear checklist and the two tags, so a finite animation anywhere else is not finished and is read at one moment, while the lab.json cleanup notes (line 87) and the solved-run record's not-covered list (line 49 at 445137e2) state 'a finite animation is finished to its end whatever its play state or delay' without that scope. My own probe on a fresh archive of the starter confirmed it: a delayed finite scale animation on the page wrapper was still in the running state after the test's finish step. Part (1) also holds: after finish() an animation that does not fill forwards leaves no effect, so the unanimated values are measured, which is Web Animations fill behaviour. In the same probe, a paused scale hold on both tags without a forwards fill drew the tags smaller before the finish step, then left no animation and an unscaled tag with drawn width equal to layout width, whereas the same hold filling both ways was caught. So 'ends at the expected values' is ambiguous at best, and with the default fill a held wrong scale passes whatever the keyframes say. The defect is maintainer and evidence wording about the owner-accepted option A residual; README line 17 and task 11 Outcome, which learners read, stay general and correct, so low severity is right. Smallest correct fix: a wording-only rewrite of that residual passage in lab.json and in the next solved-run record, with no test, README or starter change, which stays inside the approved minimal loop-6 scope and the option A decision and does not expand the contract. On the smallest fix: a general, non-exhaustive statement is preferable to extending the enumerated list again. Two successive wording loops each found the list too narrow, every further enumeration invites the same finding, and workflow 2.4 escalates a further correction loop. The general statement should say what the test does at its one measuring moment: it finishes the finite animations on the gear checklist and the two tags and measures what they then hold, which is their last keyframe only when they fill forwards and otherwise nothing at all, and it reads every other animation, on any element, as it happens to be at that moment; so any animation that changes the drawn size of the checklist or the tags at some other moment can pass. The current cases (paused, delayed or very long ones, endless ones, ones on elements around the checklist, animated custom properties) then follow as examples, introduced as examples rather than as the complete set.

Verified on the bytes at 7e1a2af6; this finding describes the same two gaps as cl8-edu-001, with full-suite reproductions on the completed work, and both are correct. (a) The finish step in tests/layout.test.mjs runs only on the gear checklist and the two tags, so finite animations on elements around the checklist, including delayed or very long forwards-filled scale-downs on ancestors, are read at one moment and can pass while the page draws the tags at another size; my probe showed such a delayed ancestor animation still running after the finish step, and the critic's controls (the same rule on the checklist or the tags fails task 11) confirm the scope. (b) What is measured after finish() is the held end, which is the last keyframe only with a forwards or both fill and otherwise the unanimated values, per Web Animations sections 4.6 and 4.4.13 cited in the finding; my probe reproduced a paused, backwards-filled scale hold on both tags that is drawn smaller but leaves nothing to measure after finishing, and the both-filled control was caught. The general opening sentence, the scoped preceding sentence and the 'elements around the checklist' category keep this low rather than medium, and README task 11 Outcome forbids every such variant. No detection change is asked for or allowed under option A.
